ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #3
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In the family tree in the lesson, Amina's father's sister is her (1 mark)
   A. cousin
   B. aunt
   C. sibling
   D. grandmother

2. Which comes first in a dictionary? (1 mark)
   A. market
   B. mango
   C. mat
   D. mother

3. What is the plural of 'monkey'? (1 mark)
   A. monkeyes
   B. monkies
   C. monkeys
   D. monkeis

4. Plural nouns: Choose the correct sentence. (1 mark)
   A. The women is selling tomatoes.
   B. The woman are selling tomatoes.
   C. The womans are selling tomatoes.
   D. The women are selling tomatoes.

5. What is the first step in writing a composition? (1 mark)
   A. Plan your ideas
   B. Write the conclusion
   C. Copy a story
   D. Draw a picture only

6. Which is the more polite request? (1 mark)
   A. Pen now.
   B. I want the pen.
   C. May I borrow your pen, please?
   D. Give me your pen.

7. The verb 'record' (to make a record) is stressed on (1 mark)
   A. both
   B. the first syllable
   C. neither
   D. the second syllable

8. An antiseptic is (1 mark)
   A. a road sign
   B. a kind of bicycle
   C. a strip of cloth
   D. a liquid or cream that kills germs on a wound

9. Pronouns: Choose the correct sentence. (1 mark)
   A. The nurse helped my.
   B. The nurse helped I.
   C. The nurse helped mine.
   D. The nurse helped me.

10. Which is better for sharing a lot of news and feelings? (1 mark)
   A. A one-word SMS
   B. A signature
   C. A letter
   D. A phone number

11. Which foods mainly give us energy? (1 mark)
   A. Vitamins only
   B. Ugali, rice and potatoes
   C. Water and tea
   D. Salt and pepper

12. Which phrase is a better word for 'nice' food? (1 mark)
   A. delicious
   B. hard
   C. bad
   D. cold

13. An email is (1 mark)
   A. a letter sent by bus
   B. a type of phone
   C. a kind of paper
   D. a message sent electronically

14. Why did Achieng tell Baraka to read his message before sending it? (1 mark)
   A. To make it longer
   B. To check the spelling
   C. To delete it
   D. To print it

15. Which word fits: 'Do you have ___ pencils?' (1 mark)
   A. any
   B. some
   C. a lot
   D. much

16. Which noun is countable? (1 mark)
   A. time
   B. money
   C. mango
   D. rice

17. Which word has the /j/ sound although it begins with the letter u? (1 mark)
   A. under
   B. umbrella
   C. uncle
   D. use

18. Which is NOT a good way to run a reading club? (1 mark)
   A. Everyone talks at once
   B. Meet at a regular time
   C. Keep a list of books read
   D. Take turns to speak

19. When do we write the word 'I' as a capital letter? (1 mark)
   A. Always
   B. Only at the start of a sentence
   C. Never
   D. Only in names

20. What is the contraction of 'do not'? (1 mark)
   A. d'not
   B. do'nt
   C. dont
   D. don't

21. What is a clinic? (1 mark)
   A. A market stall
   B. A school library
   C. A place for playing football
   D. A place where people get health care

22. Which pair differs in the sounds /s/ and /ʃ/? (1 mark)
   A. sit and seat
   B. live and leave
   C. sea and she
   D. go and no

23. Which word has the gliding vowel /əʊ/? (1 mark)
   A. sip
   B. ship
   C. bit
   D. soap

24. Which is a main idea of the text 'Keeping Clean to Stay Healthy'? (1 mark)
   A. Good hygiene keeps us healthy
   B. Soap is expensive
   C. Flies help us
   D. Germs are good for us

25. 'Who's' is a short form of which words? (1 mark)
   A. who was not
   B. who has not
   C. who is
   D. whose is

26. Which is a good way to learn a hard spelling? (1 mark)
   A. Copy it wrongly
   B. Look, cover, write and check
   C. Guess it every time
   D. Never write it

27. What is a chorus in a song? (1 mark)
   A. The name of the singer
   B. The last verse only
   C. The part repeated after each verse
   D. The first word

28. What is a diary? (1 mark)
   A. A newspaper
   B. A letter to a friend
   C. A personal record of what happens to you each day
   D. A dictionary

29. What is a good way to end a diary entry? (1 mark)
   A. With a poem only
   B. With a list of prices
   C. With a map
   D. With a plan for tomorrow or a short sign-off

30. Which sentence has a preposition of direction? (1 mark)
   A. The bank is near the school.
   B. The children walked along the road.
   C. The cat is under the chair.
   D. The book is on the desk.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Correct the sentences: (a) 'Him is a driver.' (b) 'Give the pen to she.' (c) 'The bag is mine bag.' (3 marks)

32. Use when, where, who and whose in four questions about a sports day. (4 marks)

33. Explain why reading with expression is important. (2 marks)

34. Write two words with the sound /aɪ/ and use one in a sentence. (2 marks)

35. Name the three parts of a narrative and say what goes in each. (3 marks)

36. What lesson does the poem 'The Whistle' teach about winning and losing? (2 marks)

37. Write an SMS inviting a friend to your birthday party on Saturday at 3 o'clock. (3 marks)

38. Use the words 'sibling', 'relative' and 'chore' in three sentences about a family. (3 marks)

39. Create a short puzzle with four clues whose answers are irregular plurals. (4 marks)

40. Write one statement, one WH question and one yes or no question about email. Say how the voice moves in each. (3 marks)

41. In the passage 'The Purse in the Market', what did the purse contain? (2 marks)

42. Arrange in order and write as a paragraph: (a) Finally, we went home. (b) We arrived at the farm at nine. (c) Then we fed the goats. (3 marks)

43. Write about 60 words about these pictures: (1) A boy plants a seed. (2) He waters it every day. (3) A tall plant grows. (5 marks)

44. Describe how to skim and how to scan a passage. (4 marks)

45. Write a friendly letter of about five sentences to a friend in another school about new road safety words you learnt. (5 marks)

46. Arrange in order: (a) Then she paid. (b) Grace entered the shop. (c) Finally, she went home. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #3 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — aunt
   A father's sister is an aunt.

2. B — mango
   Mango has n as the third letter, which comes before r, t and the o in mother.

3. C — monkeys
   A vowel comes before y, so just add s.

4. D — The women are selling tomatoes.
   Women is plural and takes are.

5. A — Plan your ideas
   A plan puts ideas in order first.

6. C — May I borrow your pen, please?
   It uses may I and please.

7. D — the second syllable
   The verb is re-CORD.

8. D — a liquid or cream that kills germs on a wound
   It cleans wounds by killing germs.

9. D — The nurse helped me.
   Me is the object form of I.

10. C — A letter
   A letter can hold more news.

11. B — Ugali, rice and potatoes
   They are carbohydrates.

12. A — delicious
   Delicious is a stronger, more exact word.

13. D — a message sent electronically
   Email stands for electronic mail.

14. B — To check the spelling
   Checking finds mistakes.

15. A — any
   Any is used in questions with plural nouns.

16. C — mango
   We can count mangoes.

17. D — use
   'Use' is said 'yooz', beginning with /j/.

18. A — Everyone talks at once
   A club needs turn-taking so everyone is heard.

19. A — Always
   'I' is always a capital.

20. D — don't
   The apostrophe replaces the o in 'not'.

21. D — A place where people get health care
   Clinics give health care.

22. C — sea and she
   'Sea' has /s/ and 'she' has /ʃ/.

23. D — soap
   'Soap' has /əʊ/.

24. A — Good hygiene keeps us healthy
   The whole text supports good hygiene.

25. C — who is
   Who's = who is (or who has).

26. B — Look, cover, write and check
   Cover-write-check builds memory.

27. C — The part repeated after each verse
   The chorus is repeated.

28. C — A personal record of what happens to you each day
   A diary records events and feelings.

29. D — With a plan for tomorrow or a short sign-off
   Diaries often end with plans or 'Goodnight'.

30. B — The children walked along the road.
   'Along' shows movement.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) He is a driver. (b) Give the pen to her. (c) The bag is mine. / It is my bag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: When is sports day? Where is it held? Who is the guest of honour? Whose team is winning?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct question.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: It shows the meaning and feeling of a text and makes listeners understand and enjoy it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning/feeling, 1 mark for the effect on the listener.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: kite, night. I fly my kite on Saturday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct words and 1 mark for a correct sentence.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Beginning: who, where and when. Middle: the events and problem. End: how it is solved and how people felt.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: To be a good sport: lose without crying, shake hands with the other team and say 'Good try'.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the lesson and 1 for a reason from the poem.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hi Kamau. Please come to my birthday party on Saturday at 3 o'clock at my home. Thank you. Ann.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for greeting, 1 for day, time and place, 1 for politeness and name.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: My sibling is my little sister. My aunt is a relative. My chore is to sweep the yard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: I have two of these and I walk on them: feet. You chew with these: teeth. Small animals that squeak: mice. Grown-up females: women.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each clue with a correct answer.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: I sent the email (falls). Where is the message? (falls) Did you get it? (rises)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each with correct voice movement.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: It had some coins and a card with the name Mrs Achieng Odhiambo.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the coins and 1 mark for the card.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: We arrived at the farm at nine. Then we fed the goats. Finally, we went home.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sentence in the correct place.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: One morning, Musa planted a seed in the garden. Every day he watered it. After some weeks, a small green shoot appeared. At last, a tall plant grew and Musa was proud.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for beginning, order, linking words, past tense, punctuation and length.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: To skim, look at the title, pictures and the first sentence of each paragraph to get the main idea. To scan, look quickly for key words to find a particular fact.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for skimming and 2 marks for scanning.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: A letter with address and date, Dear ..., a body that mentions words such as roundabout, foot bridge and railway crossing, a closing and a name.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for address and date, 1 for greeting, 1 for body content, 1 for closing and name, 1 for punctuation.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: b, a, c
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for b first and 1 mark for a then c.
